correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the domain (all k>=3), exact positive summands, endpoint strictness, and four-to-all-length induction. Independently proved the unique odd Zumkeller <=971 using sigma/n prime-support bounds, checked the initial even Zumkeller <=22 via divisors, and explicitly verified seven half-sum witnesses. Examined the full primary-text Proposition 4.6(a) premise. Three-summand upper uses even two-sum; 983 is excluded by 945+38. Four-summand upper covers even >=980, odd >=991, and five intervening odds. Every k>=4 lower endpoint 6k+955 forces one 945 and an impossible sum of 16 with increments 0,6,14. Induction via summand 6 gives every integer above the endpoint. Exact, independent finite arithmetic script confirms all 3<=k<=30 up to N=4000, not treated as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary paper determines two-Zumkeller-sum behavior and explicitly proposes exploring three or four summands; it contains no statement of the sharp k=3 or k>=4 thresholds. The new proof combines the known even two-sum coverage with a sharp 16-excess obstruction and five four-term witnesses, proving a single exact infinite-family law. Semantic searches and exact tables found no identical/stronger theorem; this is a relative assessment, not a novelty certification.
residual_risks: Semantic search coverage is not exhaustive; an unindexed equivalent published or unpublished formula could exist.

value.rationale: Determines the complete sharp largest-gap function for all additive lengths k>=3, including the discontinuity at k=3 and stable slope-six phase thereafter. This directly answers the three- and four-summand direction proposed in the motivating 2023 paper and extends it to every length. The sharpness is structural, requiring a unique small odd member and a minimal even-excess coin obstruction, rather than mere table reproduction; a precise natural infinite-family invariant with future use in additive representation questions. Relies on a substantive known two-sum theorem and does not claim a broadly novel general technique.
